title: Accessibility barriers can prevent travel before a trip begins for Canadians with disabilities
source_unit: Statistics Canada, Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Travel, 2025
geography: Canada; persons aged 15 years and older with disabilities or long-term conditions, with travel, daily-activity difficulty, support, and accessibility-barrier dimensions

observations.period: January 2022 to February 2025; intercity or out-of-town travel

denominator.unit: Canadian persons aged 15 years and older with disabilities or long-term conditions participating in the Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Travel

took_out_of_town_trip.unit: percent taking an out-of-town trip involving airplane, train, bus, or ferry

terminal_barrier.unit: percent of travellers experiencing at least one condition-related barrier at an airport, train station, bus terminal, or ferry terminal

vehicle_barrier.unit: percent of travellers experiencing at least one condition-related barrier inside an airplane, train, bus, or ferry

greater_daily_difficulty_trip.unit: percent taking a trip among people reporting greater difficulty with daily activities

less_daily_difficulty_trip.unit: percent taking a trip among people reporting less difficulty with daily activities

mechanism.value: Mobility access can fail at the infrastructure and service-interface stage: people may face barriers at terminals or onboard before cultural, social, consumer, or care destinations become reachable

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Canada’s official release based on the Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Travel.
observations.uncertainty: The release covers a selected population with disabilities or long-term conditions and measures self-reported travel and barriers over a multi-year reference window; it does not identify trip purpose, local travel, missed cultural events, causal effects, or the absolute number of trips prevented.
observations.subgroup: Canadians aged 15 years and older with disabilities or long-term conditions, compared by difficulty carrying out daily activities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Travel differences may reflect health, resources, trip necessity, family support, destination, or transport supply in addition to accessibility barriers; travelling does not mean the trip was easy or fully accommodated.

observations.period: January 2022 to February 2025; unmet transportation need and accommodation

denominator.unit: Canadian travellers with disabilities or long-term conditions who considered an out-of-town trip, or who needed support services or accommodations during travel

discouraged_or_prevented.unit: percent of people who considered taking a trip reporting that possible accessibility concerns discouraged or prevented an out-of-town trip

greater_difficulty_discouraged.unit: percent among people with greater difficulty carrying out daily activities

less_difficulty_discouraged.unit: percent among people with less difficulty carrying out daily activities

needed_support.unit: percent of travellers reporting that they needed support services or accommodations during their trip

full_access_to_needed_support.unit: percent among travellers needing support who had access to all support services or accommodations needed

did_not_know_how_to_request.unit: percent among people not fully accommodated citing not knowing how to request access

mechanism.value: The hidden price of mobility includes anticipated failure and administrative uncertainty: possible accessibility problems can stop a trip before purchase or departure, while request knowledge and service explanation affect whether support is realized

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the official release; support and accommodation reasons are conditional shares and multiple reasons could be selected.
observations.uncertainty: The release does not show whether a discouraged trip would have been cultural, social, medical, work-related, or recreational; reported barriers and anticipated barriers are not equivalent to observed provider failures or legal non-compliance.
observations.subgroup: Canadian persons with disabilities or long-term conditions who considered travel or needed travel support, split by daily-activity difficulty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some respondents may have adapted plans, used informal help, or chosen not to travel for reasons unrelated to accessibility; lack of knowledge about requesting support may reflect communication, planning, or provider-design issues that require separate testing.

related_sources.claim: Official Statistics Canada infographic with travel-related accessibility-barrier figures and subgroup breakdowns.
Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Travel design and collection page.
Statistics Canada accessibility statistics hub and related tables.

boundary: This record adds a transport-accessibility and anticipated-trip-prevention layer beneath cultural and social participation. It does not establish cultural-trip exclusion, causal disability effects, provider fault, legal non-compliance, trip counts, or outcomes after accommodation.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Statistics Canada release and infographic reviewed for travel incidence, terminal and onboard barriers, daily-activity gradients, support access, request knowledge, and discouraged or prevented trips.
